title.narrative: Supporting vulnerable youth to develop sustainable micro and small businesses in West Nile Region

description.narrative: 500 vulnerable youth aged 18–35 from refugee and host communities in Yumbe, Terego, and Arua districts, with 60% female participation and inclusion of persons with disabilities and young mothers. Beneficiaries include 150 start-ups and 350 existing youth-led micro and small enterprises engaged in value chains such as horticulture, poultry, apiary, cassava, simsim, and sunflower.

The overall objective is to accelerate the start-up and growth of 500 youth-owned micro- and small businesses in the refugee-hosting districts of Yumbe, Terego, and Arua (city and district) through high-quality, growth-oriented technical support, including access to finance and markets, to increase income.
Specific Objective
1. Provide 150 start-up and 350 existing youth-owned micro- and small businesses with high-quality business development support 2. To strengthen the access to markets, including cross-border trading opportunities for 150 start-up and 350 existing youth-owned micro- and small businesses 3. To unlock access to affordable growth finance for 150 start-ups and 350 existing youth-owned micro- and small businesses.

The supporting vulnerable youth to develop sustainable micro- and small businesses for enhanced resilience and economic integration in the West Nile region project seeks to accelerate the start-up and growth of youth-led micro and small enterprises in Uganda’s West Nile region, specifically in Yumbe, Terego, and Arua districts.
Despite various skilling initiatives, many young people, both refugees and host community members, struggle to transition their skills into sustainable businesses due to limited access to finance, weak market linkages, inadequate business knowledge, and the growing impact of climate change. Implemented by Cordaid in partnership with Caritas Arua Diocese, the 24-month action targets 500 vulnerable youth (60% female; 50% refugees) through a combination of reskilling, business development support, and inclusive access to finance and markets.
Focusing on key value chains such as horticulture, poultry, apiary, simsim, sunflower, and cassava, the project will strengthen youth entrepreneurship, promote climate-smart and sustainable agribusiness, and enhance economic resilience and self-reliance in refugee-hosting communities.
